answer: Distinct-History Occupancy. Each identity must hold a unique record of prior successful work in a shared ledger, verified by peers, before gaining new task rights. A newcomer starts on a jetty of probationary, low-value jobs and must complete them without dispute to advance. An attacker must sustain many such histories simultaneously; a single flagged ember of fraud voids that identity's record, forcing a restart from zero. Every sybil therefore pays the full time and labor cost of a genuine track record across a wide canyon of unverified work.
